newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE needs flexible investment laws - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: UAE needs flexible investment laws - U.S. official.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) should adopt more flexible investment laws and apply stringent copyright protection to lure foreign capital, a U.S. official said on Sunday.
"Flexibility of investment laws and commitment to copyright protection would bring in more investments to the UAE," U.S. commerce department councellor Jan Kalicki said.
Kalicki, who was speaking at a news conference in Abu Dhabi said the UAE should revise its commercial agency laws and ease regulations governing partnerships between local and foreign companies.
UAE trade law protects commercial agency agreements and requires the local partner to hold not less than 51 percent of any joint venture with a foreign party.
Kalicki said the United States was looking for investment opportunities through the Gulf state's offset programme, the free trade zones and an official bourse expected to be launched later this year.
Oil-rich UAE is eager to diversify its economy away from oil by building an industrial base and attracting foreign investments.
